To calculate the SIP amount after 30 years with a 10% step-up every year, we use the formula for compounded annual growth:

Amount in year n = Initial SIP × (1 + Step-up rate)^(n - 1)

Here:

Initial SIP = 2000

Step-up rate = 10% = 0.10

Duration = 30 years

Let's calculate it:

Amount in year 30 = 2000 × (1 + 0.10)^(30 - 1)
= 2000 × (1.10)^29

Calculating:

1.10 raised to the power of 29 is approximately 15.91.

Thus:
Amount in year 30 = 2000 × 15.91 = 31,820 INR.

After 30 years, the SIP amount will be ₹31,820 per month.

Fact check: investing ₹10k/month for 30 years totals ₹36 lakh, and ₹2k/month with 10% annual step-up totals ~₹40 lakh. By the final year, the 2k SIP grows to ~₹30k/month (inflation-adjusted ~₹5k), while the 10k SIP would be ~₹10k (~₹2k today). After 30 years, a corpus of ₹7–10 crore adjusts for inflation to ~₹1.2–1.5 crore today.

So even though the 2k step-up SIP starts small, it eventually costs much more in later years, and the difference in total investment is only ~₹20 lakh. Also, part of the invested amount loses value over time due to inflation, so the “real” invested ₹40 lakh is less in today’s terms, yet the final corpus is worth ~₹1.5 crore.
